operation_pershing_task_org.note: IMPORTANT: for Operation PERSHING (11 Feb 1967-continuing through the full reporting period), 2/8 Cav was chopped OPCON to the 1st Cav Division's OWN 3rd Brigade -- NOT its organic 1st Brigade. In exchange, 5/7 Cav (organically 3rd Brigade) was OPCON'd to 1st Brigade for the same operation. This is a genuine cross-attachment, not an OCR artifact -- it appears consistently across the two TAB A task-org listings found (Pershing and Dazzlen).

operation_dazzlem_task_org.note: Under DAZZLEM (an area-security operation running continuously since 1 Oct 66, i.e. a standing administrative/AO designation rather than a maneuver op), 2/8 Cav reverts to its organic 1st Brigade listing. Read together with the Pershing task org above, this indicates 2/8's Pershing-period OPCON to 3rd Brigade was the operationally significant one during Feb-Apr 67 combat operations.

operations.name: THAYER II
operations.note: Terminated 111315 (11 Feb) 1967 per the report; 111-day operation, longest yet conducted by the division at that point. Final body count 1757 -- highest tally for a division op to date. Only activity in this document's own reporting window (1-11 Feb) was an 82mm mortar attack on LZ English (vic BS 877013) the night of 6-7 Feb, light damage.

operations.name: PERSHING
operations.controlling_unit: multi-brigade (4 brigades committed, incl. attached 3d Bde, 25th Inf Div)
operations.mission: Reconnaissance in force onto the Bong Son Plain to spoil an assessed 22d NVA Regiment attack on LZ English during the Tet truce; continuing through end of reporting period (30 Apr 67) and beyond.
operations.results_to_date: Forced 3d NVA Division HQ and 22d NVA Regt north across the Binh Dinh/Quang Ngai border, out of the division AO.

unrelated_content_flag.note: The file also contains a fully separate, detached historical narrative -- a 1st Cav Division Office of Information and History 'Unit Historical Report' on the LZ Bird action, cover-dated 18 March 1967, describing a battle from December 1966 (LZ Bird, B/1/5 Cav, A/2/19 Arty). It names PFC Charles Abbott, C Company, 1st Battalion, 8th Cavalry (1/8 Cav -- NOT 2/8) relaying artillery fire missions. This is entirely unrelated to the March 1967 D Co KIA cluster: different unit (1/8, not 2/8), different action, different (earlier) date. Flagged here so the cover memo's '18 March 1967' date is never mistaken for an action date matching Wheeler-style KIA research; it is only the memo's transmittal date for an unrelated older report.
